title: What If You Sat in a Room Hotter Than Boiling Water?

scenes.text: What if you sat in a room hotter than boiling water? In 1775, a scientist did.
Charles Blagden stayed in a room heated to about 126 degrees Celsius for 45 minutes.
He brought a raw steak along. By the end, it was cooked.
A dog in the room endured about 113 degrees for a full hour.
Their bodies stayed far cooler than the air. Sweat evaporating quickly was the secret.
It only worked because the air was dry. Add humidity, and sweat stops cooling you.
